judge.reason: Moi and hei are both greetings; only register differs.
Only register differs: 'ok' vs 'okei' are the same word; 'Vähän väsyttää' is identical in both, so the meaning is unchanged.
Miks/miksi and sä/sinä are register differences; both ask why and whether you slept badly.

forms.lemma_meaning_en: to get, to be allowed to
forms.why_en: Saada takes -i for something that already happened, then -n for 'I': sain.
The genitive singular matches kortin: uusi becomes uuden, the si turning to de.
Adds -n for the thing you get: työpaikka becomes työpaikan, with one k.
Mahtava, great. Said alone about good news it ends in -aa: Mahtavaa!
Onni, luck, with -ksi. Onneksi olkoon means congratulations. Speech says onneks.
A wish form of olla: olkoon, may it be. Used in onneksi olkoon.
Kiitti is the everyday spoken thanks. Books write kiitos.
Speech drops the l and stretches the vowel: olen becomes oon. Books write olen. From olla, to be.
Books write todella. In speech people use tosi, 'really', instead.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
